lede: A star that pierces the dark; a drop of fluid; the Day when secrets are put to the test. Seventeen ayat join them into one claim: nothing about a person is unobserved, and the One who made him once can make him again.

names.name: al-Ṭāriq
names.note: After the oath it opens with. Ṭāriq is anyone who arrives by night, and knocks; the surah explains it at once — the piercing star.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan without disagreement: Ibn al-Jawzī records the agreement and al-Qurṭubī gives no other view. The traditional order places it thirty-sixth.
revelation.when: The middle years in Makkah, as Quraysh turned from mockery to plotting

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الطّارِقِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
سُورَةُ "الطَّارِقِ" مَكِّيَّةٌ، وَهِيَ سَبْعَ عَشْرَةَ آيَةً

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ والبَيْهَقِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ ﴿والسَّماءِ والطّارِقِ﴾ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: No occasion is reported for it. Its closing ayat fit the years in which Quraysh turned from mockery to plotting: “They are plotting a plot, and I am planning a plan. So give the disbelievers respite — leave them a while.” The Prophet ﷺ is told not to hurry their end.
Its argument for the Resurrection is the plainest in the Qurʾan. Let the human being look at what he was made from. The One who brought him out of that is able to bring him back.
aim: To show how penetrating Allah’s watch is, and how far-reaching His power.
themes: The Qurʾan as a decisive word

outline.title: The oath
outline.summary: By the sky and the night-comer — and what will make you know what the night-comer is? The piercing star. There is no soul without a guardian over it.

outline.title: Where he came from, and where he is going
outline.summary: Let man consider what he was created from: a fluid poured out, emerging from between the backbone and the ribs. He is surely able to bring him back — on the Day when secrets are put to the test, and he has no strength and no helper.

outline.title: A word that decides
outline.summary: By the sky that sends back the rain and the earth that splits with growth: this is a decisive word, and no jest. They are plotting, and I am planning. So grant the disbelievers respite; leave them for a while.

keyAyah.why: The Day everything inward is brought out. A person’s secrets — intentions, beliefs, what he hid — are what will be examined.

virtues.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite, in the noon and afternoon prayers, “By the sky with its great stars” and “By the sky and the night-comer”, and surahs like them.

before: Al-Burūj: Allah surrounds the deniers from behind. Al-Ṭāriq: over every single soul there is a keeper.
after: Al-Ṭāriq asks man to look at how he was created. Al-Aʿlā opens by glorifying the One who created and proportioned, measured and guided.

sources: The Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī; the Musnad of Aḥmad
